nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, cool summers with long daylight drive growth of grasses and shrubs; the forest line is set by cold and wind.

nodes.name: Glacial meltwater
nodes.desc: Meltwater from the Southern Patagonian Ice Field feeds the rivers and lakes of the Paine massif and the moist valleys below it.

nodes.name: Soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Thin soils of steppe, shrubland and forest hold the nutrients that plants draw up and that decomposers return.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Lenga beech
nodes.desc: Dominant tree of the Magellanic subpolar forest, tolerant of deep cold and regrowing readily after fire. Its leaves are food for South Andean deer elsewhere in Patagonia.

nodes.name: Coirón fescue
nodes.desc: The main grass of the Patagonian steppe, tolerant of wind and harsh weather; grazed by guanaco, hares and geese.

nodes.name: Prickly heath
nodes.desc: A Patagonian shrub whose berries are eaten by thrushes and other birds, which GloBI records.

nodes.name: Diddle-dee
nodes.desc: A low evergreen shrub of heath and above the tree line; GloBI records upland geese eating it.

nodes.name: Gunnera
nodes.desc: A small ground-hugging plant of damp, shaded ground, recorded as a main food of huemul in a Chilean fjord study.

nodes.name: Olive grass mouse
nodes.desc: A common small rodent of Patagonian steppe and forest; one of the many small mammals eaten by pumas, foxes and raptors.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: Introduced to the Southern Cone for hunting. It grazes grasses and herbs and is now a major prey of culpeo, pumas and raptors.

nodes.name: Upland goose
nodes.desc: Grazing goose of steppe and wetlands, feeding on leaves, stems and seeds. Foxes take many of them.

nodes.name: Austral thrush
nodes.desc: Common bird of shrubland and forest edges that eats berries such as prickly heath, and spreads their seeds.

nodes.name: Darwin's rhea
nodes.desc: A flightless bird of Patagonian scrub that eats mostly plants, plus the odd lizard or insect, and outruns predators.

nodes.name: Huemul
nodes.desc: Endangered deer of Andean forest and scrub. It browses plants such as lenga; the cougar is its only natural predator.

nodes.name: Guanaco
nodes.desc: The main large grazer, eating grasses, shrubs and herbs. Park numbers rose from about 175 in 1975 to about 3,000 by 1993.

nodes.name: Culpeo
nodes.desc: Opportunistic fox that eats hares and rodents, and sometimes young guanacos and birds.

nodes.name: Black-chested buzzard-eagle
nodes.desc: Raptor that mostly hunts mid-sized mammals, with introduced rabbits a key prey, and will take carrion when needed.

nodes.name: Southern caracara
nodes.desc: An opportunistic raptor and scavenger; GloBI records it eating hares and carrion of livestock.

nodes.name: Andean condor
nodes.desc: Mainly a scavenger on large carcasses, found by sight; it also raids nests for eggs and rarely takes small live prey.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: Top predator of the park. It preys on guanaco and huemul, and its kills feed scavengers such as condors.
